newsitem.title: USA: NYSE Jan 13-17 program trading averages 14.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE Jan 13-17 program trading averages 14.5 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading for the week of program trading averaged 14.5 percent of its average daily volume of 514.9 million shares, or 74.8 million shares, for the week Jan 13-17.
In all markets, program trading averaged 120.7 million shares a day during the week of January 13-17.

About 62 percent of program trading took place on the NYSE, 31 percent in non-U.S. markets and 7.0 percent in other domestic markets. Buy programs accounted for an average 8.2 percent, while sell programs accounted for an average 6.3 percent.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the NYSE, BNP Securities, Goldman Sachs, and Susquehanna Brokerage Services executed all or most of their program activity for customers.
Morgran Stanley and Normura Securities split its program activity between that of its own account and those of its customers.
Programing trading emcompasses a wide-range of portfolio trading strategies involving the purchase or sale of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a total value of $1 million or more.
